## Search method v007

Define X and Y exactly, including entity unit, exclusions, effective dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search and one conjunction search, using the user's broad predicate wording rather than a familiar subtype. Maintain deduplicated X/Y frontiers and an identity/evidence ledger. Also maintain a compact scope ledger: for each discovery query record added restrictions not required by the hunt (subtype, occupation, geography, era, source or familiar-name terms). A successful restricted query does not establish coverage of its parent category. Derive a few meaningful sibling partitions from source taxonomies or the eligibility definition; do not invent an exhaustive cross-product or enumerate a whole census by default. Run short discovery/check rounds, prioritizing expected verified additions per total resolution cost. Each round's neglected-subtype or reverse-frontier probe must address a specific untested scope-ledger cell or remove a recorded accidental restriction; merely paraphrasing a prior conjunction does not qualify. Check source-backed candidates on Parallel for only unresolved predicates, supplying identity and existing evidence. Use small affordable batches, price every candidate, and do not recheck established facts. No result means unresolved, not false; reject only on contradiction or an exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising ambiguous or conflicting cases individually to Exa. After two discovery searches add no plausible identities, prohibit synonymous conjunction searches and perform a residual-scope pass: identify the most consequential restriction accumulated so far, try a sibling subtype or unrestricted parent on the opposite frontier, then resolve resulting candidates before further discovery. Reserve at least 35% of initial funds for evidence and stop discovery whenever pending checks require the remaining funds. Before submitting with spare funds, perform up to three affordable residual probes covering distinct untested restrictions or source partitions, retaining enough funds to verify their likely candidates. Stop this pass after two probes add neither candidates nor useful evidence; do not spend merely to exhaust the budget. Finish with identity, predicate, subtype and effective-date audits; submit supported intersections only and never infer completeness from saturation.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['parallel'].

Price candidate batches as the sum of queries and provider charges; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Exa alone with 4 results for selected unresolved identities where ambiguity, conflicting evidence or inaccessibility warrants the higher cost. At most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, continued only if it contributes useful new identities or evidence. Try a genuinely different scope partition on Parallel before buying provider diversity for a repetitive query. Authoritative-domain filters are for targeted evidence, not general frontier coverage; relax failed filters. Use publication-date filters only when publication date itself determines eligibility, and verify effective dates in content.

### Fetch policy
Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages that can settle missing identity or predicates, and useful multi-candidate lists, rather than every result. When a list is used for scope coverage, inspect its stated subtype, date range and pagination/section links; an excerpt or one section is not an exhausted category. Follow only sections tied to a promising uncovered partition, without committing to bulk census extraction. After a blocked or uninformative page, make one targeted alternate-source attempt rather than a fetch chain.

## SiftText

SiftText is persistent memory across chats.

Entry: /Users/jack/sifttext/nodes/5e565245-14fe-406c-977c-cf94a9be246b/node.md
Retrieval guide: /Users/jack/sifttext/nodes/526ed0f5-4e5d-42b3-9e3f-b7ad429f2df8/node.md

At the start of every new chat, unless I say not to use SiftText, before any other tool call:
1. Run `sifttext instructions`.
2. Read the Entry above and follow it, plus any `agent-instructions` the command returns.
3. Before retrieving knowledge, read the Retrieval guide above, do not search first.

## Tooling policy

- Never directly invoke `python`, `python3`, `pip`, or `pip3` unless explicitly instructed by the human.
- Use `uv` for all agent-initiated Python work:
  - Python execution: `uv run python ...`
  - Scripts and tests: `uv run ...`
  - Throwaway dependencies: `uv run --with <package> ...`
  - Python CLI tools: `uvx <tool>`
  - Durable project dependencies: use the project's appropriate `uv` command and preserve its lockfile.
- For non-Python probing or testing with unavailable tools:
  - One executable: `nix run nixpkgs#<package> -- <args>`
  - Temporary environment: `nix shell nixpkgs#<package> ... --command <command>`
- Nix environments are temporary, but downloaded store paths may remain cached until garbage collection.
- If a Nix dependency becomes useful for recurring or future work, tell the human and suggest adding it to the appropriate durable Nix configuration (such as a project flake/dev shell, Home Manager, or nix-darwin configuration). Do not make that durable change unless asked.

</addendum>

|caption=Distribution of named [[Impact crater|craters]] in the [[Solar System]] {{as of|2017|lc=y}}{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} }} This is a list of named [[Impact crater|craters]] on [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], the [[Inner planets|innermost planet]] of the [[Solar System]] ''(for other features, see [[list of geological features on Mercury]])''. Most Mercurian craters [[Planetary nomenclature|are named after]] famous writers, artists and composers. According to the rules by IAU's [[Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature]], all new craters must be named after an artist that was famous for more than fifty years, and dead for more than three years, before the date they are named. Craters larger than 250 km in diameter are referred to as "basins" ''(also see {{Section link||Terminology}})''.[https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/Projects/PlanetaryMapping/DIGGEOL/mercury/h7/h7.pdf H-7 text\_all.word] {{As of|2025}}, there are 444 named Mercurian craters, a small fraction of the total number of named Solar System craters, most of which are [[List of craters on the Moon|lunar]], [[List of craters on Mars|Martian]] and [[List of craters on Venus|Venerian]] craters.{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [[Callisto (moon)|Callisto]] ([[List of craters on Callisto|141]]), [[Ganymede (moon)|Ganymede]] ([[List of craters on Ganymede|131]]), [[Rhea (moon)|Rhea]] (128), [[4 Vesta|Vesta]] (90), [[Ceres (dwarf planet)|Ceres]] (90), [[Dione (moon)|Dione]] (73), [[Iapetus (moon)|Iapetus]] (58), [[Enceladus (moon)|Enceladus]] (53), [[Tethys (moon)|Tethys]] (50) and [[Europa (moon)|Europa]] ([[List of craters on Europa|41]]). |caption=Distribution of named [[Impact crater|craters]] in the [[Solar System]] {{as of|2017|lc=y}}{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} }} This is a list of named [[Impact crater|craters]] on [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], the [[Inner planets|innermost planet]] of the [[Solar System]] ''(for other features, see [[list of geological features on Mercury]])''. Most Mercurian craters [[Planetary nomenclature|are named after]] famous writers, artists and composers. According to the rules by IAU's [[Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature]], all new craters must be named after an artist that was famous for more than fifty years, and dead for more than three years, before the date they are named. Craters larger than 250 km in diameter are referred to as "basins" ''(also see {{Section link||Terminology}})''.[https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/Projects/PlanetaryMapping/DIGGEOL/mercury/h7/h7.pdf H-7 text\_all.word] {{As of|2025}}, there are 444 named Mercurian craters, a small fraction of the total number of named Solar System craters, most of which are [[List of craters on the Moon|lunar]], [[List of craters on Mars|Martian]] and [[List of craters on Venus|Venerian]] craters.{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [[Callisto (moon)|Callisto]] ([[List of craters on Callisto|141]]), [[Ganymede (moon)|Ganymede]] ([[List of craters on Ganymede|131]]), [[Rhea (moon)|Rhea]] (128), [[4 Vesta|Vesta]] (90), [[Ceres (dwarf planet)|Ceres]] (90), [[Dione (moon)|Dione]] (73), [[Iapetus (moon)|Iapetus]] (58), [[Enceladus (moon)|Enceladus]] (53), [[Tethys (moon)|Tethys]] (50) and [[Europa (moon)|Europa]] ([[List of craters on Europa|41]]). |caption=Distribution of named [[Impact crater|craters]] in the [[Solar System]] {{as of|2017|lc=y}}{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} }} This is a list of named [[Impact crater|craters]] on [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], the [[Inner planets|innermost planet]] of the [[Solar System]] ''(for other features, see [[list of geological features on Mercury]])''. Most Mercurian craters [[Planetary nomenclature|are named after]] famous writers, artists and composers. According to the rules by IAU's [[Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature]], all new craters must be named after an artist that was famous for more than fifty years, and dead for more than three years, before the date they are named. Craters larger than 250 km in diameter are referred to as "basins" ''(also see {{Section link||Terminology}})''.[https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/Projects/PlanetaryMapping/DIGGEOL/mercury/h7/h7.pdf H-7 text\_all.word] {{As of|2025}}, there are 444 named Mercurian craters, a small fraction of the total number of named Solar System craters, most of which are [[List of craters on the Moon|lunar]], [[List of craters on Mars|Martian]] and [[List of craters on Venus|Venerian]] craters.{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [[Callisto (moon)|Callisto]] ([[List of craters on Callisto|141]]), [[Ganymede (moon)|Ganymede]] ([[List of craters on Ganymede|131]]), [[Rhea (moon)|Rhea]] (128), [[4 Vesta|Vesta]] (90), [[Ceres (dwarf planet)|Ceres]] (90), [[Dione (moon)|Dione]] (73), [[Iapetus (moon)|Iapetus]] (58), [[Enceladus (moon)|Enceladus]] (53), [[Tethys (moon)|Tethys]] (50) and [[Europa (moon)|Europa]] ([[List of craters on Europa|41]]). |caption=Distribution of named [[Impact crater|craters]] in the [[Solar System]] {{as of|2017|lc=y}}{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} }} This is a list of named [[Impact crater|craters]] on [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], the [[Inner planets|innermost planet]] of the [[Solar System]] ''(for other features, see [[list of geological features on Mercury]])''. Most Mercurian craters [[Planetary nomenclature|are named after]] famous writers, artists and composers. According to the rules by IAU's [[Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature]], all new craters must be named after an artist that was famous for more than fifty years, and dead for more than three years, before the date they are named. Craters larger than 250 km in diameter are referred to as "basins" ''(also see {{Section link||Terminology}})''.[https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/Projects/PlanetaryMapping/DIGGEOL/mercury/h7/h7.pdf H-7 text\_all.word] {{As of|2025}}, there are 444 named Mercurian craters, a small fraction of the total number of named Solar System craters, most of which are [[List of craters on the Moon|lunar]], [[List of craters on Mars|Martian]] and [[List of craters on Venus|Venerian]] craters.{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [[Callisto (moon)|Callisto]] ([[List of craters on Callisto|141]]), [[Ganymede (moon)|Ganymede]] ([[List of craters on Ganymede|131]]), [[Rhea (moon)|Rhea]] (128), [[4 Vesta|Vesta]] (90), [[Ceres (dwarf planet)|Ceres]] (90), [[Dione (moon)|Dione]] (73), [[Iapetus (moon)|Iapetus]] (58), [[Enceladus (moon)|Enceladus]] (53), [[Tethys (moon)|Tethys]] (50) and [[Europa (moon)|Europa]] ([[List of craters on Europa|41]]). ## Nomenclature News

#### Name Approved for Io: Aganjú Fluctus

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Aganjú Fluctus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16518) for a feature on Io. For more information, please see the [Io nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/io_comp_color.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

## Nomenclature News

#### Name Approved for Io: Aganjú Fluctus

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Aganjú Fluctus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16518) for a feature on Io. For more information, please see the [Io nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/io_comp_color.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Mars: Merchant, Ilgenfritz, and Reine

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Merchant](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16515), [Ilgenfritz](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16516), and [Reine](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16517) for three craters on Mars. For more information, please see the [MC-27](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc27_2014.pdf) and [MC-29](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc29_2014.pdf) nomenclature maps in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Mercury: Mangeshkar, Ashevak, Nwapa, Montgomery, Na Hye-sŏk, Noonuccal, and Albizu

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Mangeshkar](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16508), [Ashevak](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16509), [Nwapa](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16510), [Montgomery](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16511), [Na Hye-sŏk](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16512), [Noonuccal](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16513), and [Albizu](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16514) for seven features on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-4](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-4.pdf), [H-5](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-5.pdf), [H-9](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-9.pdf), [H-10](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-10.pdf), and [H-11](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-11.pdf) nomenclature quad maps in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for a Ring Arc of Neptune: Sincérité

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name Sincérité for a ring arc of Neptune. For more information, please see the [Ring and Ring Gap Nomenclature page](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Page/Rings) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Donaldjohanson: Natunuku Dorsum

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Natunuku Dorsum](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16507) for a feature on Donaldjohanson. For more information, please see the [Donaldjohanson nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/donaldjohanson.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Mercury: Mirabilis Rupes

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Mirabilis Rupes](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16506) for a feature on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-11 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-11.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for the Moon: McLaughlin D

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [McLaughlin D](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16505) for a feature on the Moon. For more information, please see the [LAC-21 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Lunar/lac_21_wac.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Enceladus: Euphrates Sulcus and Fars Sulcus

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Euphrates Sulcus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16503) and [Fars Sulcus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16504)
for two features on Enceladus. For more information, please see the [Enceladus nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/enceladus_comp.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Mars: Pals

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Pals](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16502) for a feature on Mars. #### Names Approved for Dione: Hector and Andromache

## Nomenclature News

#### Name Approved for Io: Aganjú Fluctus

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Aganjú Fluctus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16518) for a feature on Io. For more information, please see the [Io nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/io_comp_color.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Mars: Merchant, Ilgenfritz, and Reine

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Merchant](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16515), [Ilgenfritz](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16516), and [Reine](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16517) for three craters on Mars. For more information, please see the [MC-27](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc27_2014.pdf) and [MC-29](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc29_2014.pdf) nomenclature maps in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Mercury: Mangeshkar, Ashevak, Nwapa, Montgomery, Na Hye-sŏk, Noonuccal, and Albizu

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Mangeshkar](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16508), [Ashevak](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16509), [Nwapa](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16510), [Montgomery](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16511), [Na Hye-sŏk](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16512), [Noonuccal](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16513), and [Albizu](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16514) for seven features on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-4](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-4.pdf), [H-5](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-5.pdf), [H-9](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-9.pdf), [H-10](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-10.pdf), and [H-11](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-11.pdf) nomenclature quad maps in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for a Ring Arc of Neptune: Sincérité

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name Sincérité for a ring arc of Neptune. For more information, please see the [Ring and Ring Gap Nomenclature page](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Page/Rings) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Donaldjohanson: Natunuku Dorsum

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Natunuku Dorsum](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16507) for a feature on Donaldjohanson. For more information, please see the [Donaldjohanson nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/donaldjohanson.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Mercury: Mirabilis Rupes

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Mirabilis Rupes](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16506) for a feature on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-11 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-11.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for the Moon: McLaughlin D

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [McLaughlin D](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16505) for a feature on the Moon. For more information, please see the [LAC-21 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Lunar/lac_21_wac.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Enceladus: Euphrates Sulcus and Fars Sulcus

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Euphrates Sulcus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16503) and [Fars Sulcus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16504)
for two features on Enceladus. For more information, please see the [Enceladus nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/enceladus_comp.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Mars: Pals

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Pals](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16502) for a feature on Mars. For more information, please see the [MC-4 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc4_2014.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Dione: Hector and Andromache

## Nomenclature News

* #### Name Approved for the Moon: Mons Kocher



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Mons Kocher](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16394) for a feature on the Moon. For more information, please see the [LAC-144 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Lunar/lac_144_wac.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

  + Moon
* #### Seven Names Approved for Mercury: Mahsati, We'wha, Lucena, Rainey, Guinness, Price, and Traba



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Mahsati](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16387), [We’wha](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16388), [Lucena](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16389), [Rainey](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16390), [Guinness](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16391), [Price](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16392), and [Traba](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16393) for seven craters on Mercury.

  + Mercury
* #### Name Approved for Mercury: Serp Facula



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Serp Facula](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16386) for a feature on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-10 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-10.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

  + Mercury

  + Mars

For more information, please see the [Titan North Pole nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/titan_northpole_new.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Mercury: Bulsara

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Bulsara](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16280) for a crater on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-14 quad nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-14.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Mars: Taung

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Taung](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16279) for a feature on Mars. For more information, please see the [MC-11 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc11_2014.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Mars: Kahnawake, Longwood, and Otepa

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Kahnawake](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16276), [Longwood](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16277) , and [Otepa](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16278) for three features on Mars. For more information, please see the [MC-16 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc16_2014.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for Rhea: Okikurumi

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Okikurumi](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16275) for a feature on Rhea. For more information, please see the [Rhea nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/rhea_comp.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

## Search method v007

Define X and Y exactly, including entity unit, exclusions, effective dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search and one conjunction search, using the user's broad predicate wording rather than a familiar subtype. Maintain deduplicated X/Y frontiers and an identity/evidence ledger. Also maintain a compact scope ledger: for each discovery query record added restrictions not required by the hunt (subtype, occupation, geography, era, source or familiar-name terms). A successful restricted query does not establish coverage of its parent category. Derive a few meaningful sibling partitions from source taxonomies or the eligibility definition; do not invent an exhaustive cross-product or enumerate a whole census by default. Run short discovery/check rounds, prioritizing expected verified additions per total resolution cost. According to the rules by IAU's [[Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature]], all new craters must be named after an artist that was famous for more than fifty years, and dead for more than three years, before the date they are named. Craters larger than 250 km in diameter are referred to as "basins" ''(also see {{Section link||Terminology}})''.[https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/Projects/PlanetaryMapping/DIGGEOL/mercury/h7/h7.pdf H-7 text\_all.word] {{As of|2025}}, there are 444 named Mercurian craters, a small fraction of the total number of named Solar System craters, most of which are [[List of craters on the Moon|lunar]], [[List of craters on Mars|Martian]] and [[List of craters on Venus|Venerian]] craters.{{efn|name=WGPSN-Dropped}} Other, non-planetary bodies with numerous named craters include [[Callisto (moon)|Callisto]] ([[List of craters on Callisto|141]]), [[Ganymede (moon)|Ganymede]] ([[List of craters on Ganymede|131]]), [[Rhea (moon)|Rhea]] (128), [[4 Vesta|Vesta]] (90), [[Ceres (dwarf planet)|Ceres]] (90), [[Dione (moon)|Dione]] (73), [[Iapetus (moon)|Iapetus]] (58), [[Enceladus (moon)|Enceladus]] (53), [[Tethys (moon)|Tethys]] (50) and [[Europa (moon)|Europa]] ([[List of craters on Europa|41]]). ## Nomenclature News

#### Name Approved for Io: Aganjú Fluctus

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Aganjú Fluctus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16518) for a feature on Io. For more information, please see the [Io nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/io_comp_color.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Mars: Merchant, Ilgenfritz, and Reine

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Merchant](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16515), [Ilgenfritz](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16516), and [Reine](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16517) for three craters on Mars. For more information, please see the [MC-27](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc27_2014.pdf) and [MC-29](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc29_2014.pdf) nomenclature maps in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Names Approved for Mercury: Mangeshkar, Ashevak, Nwapa, Montgomery, Na Hye-sŏk, Noonuccal, and Albizu

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Mangeshkar](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16508), [Ashevak](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16509), [Nwapa](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16510), [Montgomery](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16511), [Na Hye-sŏk](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16512), [Noonuccal](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16513), and [Albizu](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16514) for seven features on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-4](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-4.pdf), [H-5](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-5.pdf), [H-9](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-9.pdf), [H-10](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-10.pdf), and [H-11](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-11.pdf) nomenclature quad maps in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

#### Name Approved for a Ring Arc of Neptune: Sincérité

The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name Sincérité for a ring arc of Neptune. For more information, please see the [Ring and Ring Gap Nomenclature page](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Page/Rings) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

## Nomenclature News

* #### Name Approved for the Moon: Mons Kocher



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Mons Kocher](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16394) for a feature on the Moon. For more information, please see the [LAC-144 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Lunar/lac_144_wac.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

  + Moon
* #### Seven Names Approved for Mercury: Mahsati, We'wha, Lucena, Rainey, Guinness, Price, and Traba



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Mahsati](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16387), [We’wha](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16388), [Lucena](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16389), [Rainey](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16390), [Guinness](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16391), [Price](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16392), and [Traba](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16393) for seven craters on Mercury.

  + Mercury
* #### Name Approved for Mercury: Serp Facula



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the name [Serp Facula](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16386) for a feature on Mercury. For more information, please see the [H-10 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/H-10.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

  + Mercury
* #### Thirteen Names Approved for Mars



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Forro](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16373), [Sidhi](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16374), [Lendringsen](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16375), [Pizzarello](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16376), [Minami](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16377), [Idah](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16378), [Knudsen](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16379), [Drake](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16380), [Moyo](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16381), [Papike](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16382), [Townsend](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16383), [Blount](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16384), and [Tupã](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16385) for thirteen features on Mars. For more information, please see the [MC-27 nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/mc27_2014.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

  + Mars
* #### Names Approved for Io: Amatsumara Patera, Antenora Mons, Cocytus Montes, Dis Mons, and Guaraci Fluctus



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Amatsumara Patera](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16371), [Antenora Mons](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16369), [Cocytus Montes](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16370), [Dis Mons](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16368), and [Guaraci Fluctus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16372) for five features on Io. For more information, please see the [Io nomenclature map](https://asc-planetarynames-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/io_comp_color.pdf) in the [Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/).

  + Io
* #### Names Approved for Pluto: Gibson and Giclas



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Gibson](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16366) and [Giclas](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16367) for two craters on Pluto.

  + Pluto
* #### Names Approved for Selam



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Piękna Lobus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16363) and [Lẹwa Lobus](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16364) for the two lobes of Selam, and the surface feature name [Uwoduhi Dorsum](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16365) for a dorsum.

  + Selam
* #### Names Approved for Dinkinesh



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Totoka Saxum](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16358), [Fab Dorsum](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16359), [Bella Dorsum](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16360), [Sumak Fossa](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16361), and [Indah Fossa](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16362) for five features on Dinkinesh.

  + Dinkinesh
* #### Names Approved for Triton: Yara, Xuuch, and Unga



  The IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature has approved the names [Yara](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16355), [Xuuch](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16356), and [Unga](https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16357) for three features on Triton.

  + Triton
* #### Names Approved for Mercury: Codesido, Wu Shujuan, El Husseini, Freire, Asawa, Halim, Bilokur, and Le Guin
